id: title:a-lider:match invites case insensitively for saml and jit signups

review.posthog_relevance: These hunks demonstrate a localized, bounded change to SAML and social-domain invitation workflows, replacing exact email matching with case-insensitive matching. This could prevent account creation failures for users whose invited and account emails differ only in case, while the supplied hunks do not establish broader systemic risk reduction or unverified adoption.
review.reason: The supplied hunks show a substantive, bounded correctness improvement: P1.F1.H1 and P1.F1.H2 replace exact email matching with case-insensitive matching in SAML and social-domain provisioning, potentially fixing signup failures. P1.F2.H2 updates a test helper to use an asserted email, improving maintainability. This warrants a score of 1, not 3, because the implementation and its
review.uncertainty: The supplied hunks are not a complete chunk, and the observations do not establish unverified outcomes such as actual incident avoidance or widespread adoption. The tier is assigned based on the observed bounded change, not on unverified benefits.

observations.limitations: All supplied hunks are from P1, which is not a complete chunk. No score can be assigned.

observations.behavior: The lookup_invite_for_saml function now uses target_email__iexact instead of target_email, allowing case-insensitive matching.
observations.posthog_connection: This could allow SAML-invited users with mismatched email casing to successfully claim an invite, potentially fixing a signup failure.

observations.behavior: The process_social_domain_jit_provisioning_signup function now uses target_email__iexact instead of target_email, allowing case-insensitive matching.
observations.posthog_connection: This could allow social-domain-invited users with mismatched email casing to successfully claim an invite, potentially fixing a signup failure.

observations.behavior: The run_test_for_allowed_domain test helper now accepts an asserted_email parameter, and the mocked response uses this parameter instead of a hardcoded email.
observations.posthog_connection: This makes the test more maintainable and less brittle, allowing the test to use the asserted email rather than a hardcoded value.
